priceSnapshot.note: Down 2.21 percent on the 24h open of 80,734.1, but UP 394.2 points - 0.50 percent - against the 78,553.0 endday read six hours and thirty-eight minutes ago. Those two numbers describe the same market and both matter. The 24h window still contains the 80,755.7 high and the whole 2,901.6 point unwind that followed it, so the day is unambiguously red. The last eight hours, though, are a base: after the 77,854.1 capitulation low at 21:00Z, price has traded a 78,308.8 to 79,244.8 range for eight consecutive hourly bars without revisiting the low. Spot sits 1,093.1 points above that low and 1,786.9 below the 24h open, which is almost exactly the middle of the day's damage. Endday's ADD gate at a settled 1H close above 79,003.0 FIRED at 02:00Z with a 79,108.4 close and was confirmed by 79,087.3 at 03:00Z; endday's reduce gate at 78,308.8 did not fire, the 00:00Z bar wicked to exactly 78,308.8 and closed 78,632.0. Price has since faded back to 55.8 points below the fired add level, so the gate is right and the follow-through is not there yet.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $78,635.7 AND a failure to reclaim it on either of the next two hourly bars. That is the low of the 05:00Z bar and it sits 21.1 points under the 15m EMA200 at 78,656.6, the moving average that flipped from floor to ceiling during yesterday's break and has now been reclaimed as a floor again. Losing it would say the reclaim failed. Spot is 311.5 points above it, 0.59 hourly ATRs at the current 531.32. The two-bar reclaim clause is retained - it filtered three false triggers in a single day yesterday and it is the single most valuable piece of machinery this desk has built.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $79,244.8, the high of the 02:00Z bar and the ceiling of the eight-hour base. Clearing it on a close would take out the base top and put price directly into the 79,250 liquidation bucket, which holds 1,273,828 USD of liquidations that are 100.0 percent SHORT - the first meaningful short-side fuel to appear anywhere on the board in two days. Spot is 297.6 points below it, 0.56 hourly ATRs.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from endday's REDUCE to ADD, and the reason is that endday's OWN add gate fired. It required a settled 1H close above 79,003.0; the 02:00Z bar closed 79,108.4, clearing it by 105.4 points, and the 03:00Z bar closed 79,087.3 to confirm rather than reject. Endday's reduce gate at 78,308.8 did not fire - the 00:00Z bar traded to exactly 78,308.8 and closed 78,632.0, 323.2 points above it. Three further things have improved. FIRST, price has reclaimed the 1H EMA50 at 78,761.8, which endday recorded as lost by 138.1 points and which spot is now 185.4 points above, and it has reclaimed the 15m EMA200 at 78,656.6 that had flipped to resistance. SECOND, the 1H MACD histogram has crossed positive for the first time since the breakdown: minus 52.81, minus 25.17, minus 22.98, minus 3.24, plus 0.91, plus 4.04. THIRD, the 25 August ETF print, which endday could not grade because IBIT was still showing a dash, has landed at plus 314.3m with IBIT supplying 284.4m of it - the seventh consecutive inflow day and 2,569.7m over the streak. The honest limits on this are stated in full below and they are why the add is 20 USDT of idle cash and not a leveraged position: the 4H MACD histogram at minus 305.55 is the worst reading of the entire leg, the daily RSI at 83.43 is still deeply overbought, and spot has already faded 297.6 points back off the base high.

liquidation.note: 3,250,128 USD across 175 fills and 100.0 percent of it LONG - not a single short liquidation in the bucket. It remains the heaviest cluster on the whole 18-hour board and it now sits 947.2 points below spot, 1.78 hourly ATRs, which is materially further away than the 553.0 points endday measured. Flagged as the magnet on size and one-sidedness. The same caveat governs how it should be weighted, and it has grown stronger overnight: this is REALIZED liquidation history, all of it stamped 21:08Z or earlier, and nothing has been added to it in the ten hours since. That is spent fuel. Yesterday's midday learned the hard way that spent fuel is not the same as no fuel, so it stays on the board - but a second visit finds a thinner book than 3.25m implies.

2,382,174 USD across 279 fills, 2,374,292 of it long against 7,882 short - a 301-to-1 tilt. Endday measured this bucket at 2,382,174 USD with the newest fill stamped 00:10:15Z and called it a live process. It has taken NO new fills since: the total is unchanged to the dollar across six and a half hours. The shelf that was actively burning at the endday snapshot has gone quiet, which is the single most constructive change on this board.

2,157,564 USD across 306 fills, 2,120,003 long against 37,561 short, a 56-to-1 tilt. Sits 447.2 points below spot, 0.84 hourly ATRs, and is the first heavy level under the reduce gate at 78,635.7. If the gate fails this is what price is falling into.

1,702,181 USD across 375 fills - the highest fill count anywhere on the board - split 1,160,312 long against 541,869 short. That 2.14-to-1 ratio is by far the most balanced of any bucket below spot, and it is the level the market has spent the last eight hours grinding across. Two-sided liquidations in a tight range are the signature of a base being built rather than a floor being broken. It sits 197.2 points below spot, on top of the 1H EMA50 at 78,761.8.

785,559 USD across 182 fills, 279,251 long against 506,308 short - the first bucket on the board where SHORTS were the majority of the pain. Spot at 78,947.2 is sitting 52.8 points underneath it. Classified as below because spot is fractionally under the bucket centre, but in practice this is the level price is standing on.

1,273,828 USD across 158 fills and 100.0 percent of it SHORT - the mirror image of the 78,000 bucket and the single most important new feature on this board. Endday's report had no meaningful short-side cluster anywhere; this one was built entirely during the overnight recovery as shorts opened into the bounce and were run over. It sits 302.8 points above spot, 0.57 hourly ATRs, and it is exactly where the add gate at 79,244.8 lives. That coincidence is the whole bull case in one line: a settled close through the base high lands straight into 1.27m of short liquidations with nothing above them until 79,500.

339,034 USD across 61 fills, 100.0 percent short. Thin, but it is the second short-side level above spot and it sits just under the 79,571.4 resistance that has capped every attempt since midday yesterday. If the 79,250 bucket goes, this is the next stop and it will not offer much resistance on its own.

divergences.note: The divergence endday flagged as its honest counterweight has now RESOLVED, and it resolved in the direction it pointed. At the 20:00Z bar price made a low of 78,174.5 with the 1H MACD histogram at minus 177.41 and RSI at 39.42. At 21:00Z price made a LOWER low of 77,854.1, 320.4 points beneath it, while the histogram made a HIGHER low at minus 172.82 and RSI made a higher low at 44.24. Both oscillators refused to confirm the new price low. Price is now 1,093.1 points above that low and the histogram has crossed positive at plus 4.04. Recorded here because a divergence that pays is worth the same scrutiny as one that fails: endday priced this correctly, named it explicitly as the reason its REDUCE was 10 percent rather than a real exit, and was right to do so. No NEW divergence is present on any timeframe at this snapshot.

calibration.rollingRecord: Grading endday against this 02:13 COT read of 78,947.2. Endday trimmed 10 percent of the spot core at 78,553.0 and spot is 394.2 points higher, so the trim is out of the money by 0.50 percent on a tenth of the book - roughly 0.07 USDT. That completes yesterday's card at 1 correct in 4: midnight bought 20 USDT at 80,726.8 and is down 2.21 percent; morning trimmed at 79,161.2 and is now down 0.27 percent, so even the day's one winner has since gone red; midday bought 18 USDT at 79,140.7 and is down 0.24 percent; endday trimmed at 78,553.0 and is down 0.50 percent. Every one of the four sessions is now underwater against this mark. The honest reading of that is not that the desk was directionally wrong four times - it is that it traded a 2,900 point round trip four times and captured none of it, because each session acted at the point of maximum local conviction rather than at the edges.
calibration.note: Endday's REDUCE gate at a settled 1H close below 78,308.8 did NOT fire, and it was close: the 00:00Z bar traded to EXACTLY 78,308.8, to the tick, and closed 78,632.0. A wick to the level is not a close below it, so the gate held and the two-bar reclaim clause was never even needed. Endday's ADD gate at a settled 1H close above 79,003.0 DID fire, at 02:00Z with a 79,108.4 close clearing it by 105.4 points, confirmed by 79,087.3 at 03:00Z. This is the FIRST add gate this desk has fired in the eight-session window and it is why this session adds rather than waits. Endday's invalidation at 77,854.1 was never revisited; the lowest print since publication is 78,308.8, some 454.7 points above it. acting_helped is FALSE for the trim itself. The transferable finding is about gate quality rather than direction: endday wrote a reduce gate and an add gate that were 694.2 points apart around a 78,553.0 spot, the add gate fired within four hours, and the desk's own trim was on the wrong side of it. When a session sets a tight two-sided gate and then acts against one of its own sides before the market chooses, the gate was doing better work than the trade.
